  task new_data  (  output bit is_valid , output int handle , input string data_class  ) 

Command Support: Used to create a new data instance.

is_valid - Functions as a return value ('0' only if the data_class argument is not recognized).

handle - Assigned with a pointer to the new data object resulting from the new_data operation.

data_class - String identifier of the new data instance

  task apply_data  (  output bit is_valid , input int handle , bit delete_handle = 1  ) 

Command Support: Used to accept the contents of a data object and have them applied by the model.

is_valid - Functions as a return value ('0' only if the handle argument is not valid).

handle - The pointer of the data object to be applied.

delete_handle - Flag that determines if the handle should be automatically deleted once the object is submitted to the model.

  task delete_data  (  output bit is_valid , input int handle  ) 

Command Support: Used to delete the handle associated with an active data object.

is_valid - Functions as a return value ('0' only if the handle argument does not point to a valid data object).

handle - The pointer of the data object to be deleted.

  task copy_data  (  output bit is_valid , output int handle , input int src_handle  ) 

Command Support: Instructs the model to make a (deep) copy of the data object referenced by the src_handle argument, store it as a new data object, and assign the the handle var argument with a pointer to the new copy.

is_valid - Functions as a return value ('0' only if the src_handle argument does not point to a valid data object).

handle - Assigned with a pointer to the new data object resulting from the copy operation.

src_handle - The pointer to the data object to be copied.

  task display_data  (  output bit is_valid , input int handle , string prefix  ) 

Command Support: Instructs the transactor to display (to log or transcript) the contents of the data object associated with the given handle. If there is no valid data object associated with the handle, the is_valid argument is assigned to 0, and the task returns without further action.

is_valid - Functions as a return value ('0' only if the handle argument does not point to a valid data object).

handle - Identifies the data object to be displayed.

prefix - This string prepended to each line of the resulting display.

  task get_data_prop  (  output bit is_valid , input int handle , string prop_name , output bit [1023:0] prop_val , input int array_ix  ) 

Command Support: Retrieves the value (into the prop_val var argument) of a specified public property, in the data object pointed to by the handle argument.

If the prop_name represents a sub-object, this task stores a reference to that sub-object as an data object, and assigns the prop_val argument with an int that is a handle to that sub-object. It is the user's responsibility to manage references to such sub-objects.

If the value passed in to the handle argument is equal to `SVT_CMD_NULL_HANDLE then the prop_name argument represents a property that is handled by the component that is the target of the get_data_prop() call. The following properties are recognized by all components:

"name"
Returns the class name of the target component.
"instance"
Returns the fully qualified instance name of the target component.
"verbosity"
Returns the configured verbosity value. The values that are returned correspond to the following macro constants:
`SVT_CMD_NONE_VERBOSITY
`SVT_CMD_NORMAL_VERBOSITY
`SVT_CMD_TRACE_VERBOSITY
`SVT_CMD_DEBUG_VERBOSITY
`SVT_CMD_VERBOSE_VERBOSITY
"max_error_count"
Returns the configured number of errors allowed before the test automatically shuts down.
"fatal_count"
Returns the number of fatal severity messages issued.
"error_count"
Returns the number of error severity messages issued.
"warning_count"
Returns the number of warning severity messages issued.

is_valid - Functions as a return value ('0' if the handle argument does not point to a data object that is currently active, or if the property specified by the prop_name argument does not exist in that object, or if the property is an array but the index specified by the array_ix argument is out of bounds).

handle - Identifies the data object whose property is to be accessed.

prop_name - Identifies the property name whose value is to be retrieved.

prop_val - Functions as the return value (the value of the specified property). Note: Regardless of its actual type in the data object, the property value is converted to a 1Kb bit-vector. This return value must be dealt with in a manner applicable to the actual property type by the command code. For instance, the command code must understand the int equivalents of enumerated type values in the data object.

array_ix - Specifies the array element to be accessed if the property is an array. This argument is required, but is ignored if the property is not an array. If this argument is out of the array bounds in the object, an error is reported.

  task set_data_prop  (  output bit is_valid , input int handle , string prop_name , bit [1023:0] prop_val , int array_ix  ) 

Command Support: Sets the value provided by the prop_val argument of a specified public property, in the data object pointed to by the handle argument.

This command is used to first set up a model's Instance Name, and subsequently to set the value of a property in temporary data object currently available within the transactor. The first time this task is called by the testbench, it must be called with the prop_name argument of "instance" and a prop_val argument value representing the Instance Name of the model (component) for the model (component). It is based on this first call to this task, that the model is initialized. All subsequent calls to this task should be for the purpose of setting the values of properties in temporary data objects currently valid within the transactor.

If the value passed in to the handle argument is equal to `SVT_CMD_NULL_HANDLE then the prop_name argument represents a property that is handled by the component that is the target of the set_data_prop() call. The following properties are recognized by all components:

"instance"
Sets the instance name of the target component.
"verbosity"
Sets the verbosity value. The values that are accepted for the prop_val argument correspond to the following macro constants:
`SVT_CMD_NONE_VERBOSITY
`SVT_CMD_NORMAL_VERBOSITY
`SVT_CMD_TRACE_VERBOSITY
`SVT_CMD_DEBUG_VERBOSITY
`SVT_CMD_VERBOSE_VERBOSITY
"max_error_count"
Sets the number of errors allowed before the test automatically shuts down.
"filter(<message_text>)"
Sets up or clears a message filter. The message_text string is matched using regex against all messages issued by the targeted component. The severity of the message will be changed to the provided severity if the string matches. The following values are recognized as the prop_val value:
`SVT_CMD_FATAL_SEVERITY
`SVT_CMD_ERROR_SEVERITY
`SVT_CMD_WARNING_SEVERITY
`SVT_CMD_NORMAL_SEVERITY
`SVT_CMD_TRACE_SEVERITY
`SVT_CMD_DEBUG_SEVERITY
`SVT_CMD_VERBOSE_SEVERITY
`SVT_CMD_CLEAR_SEVERITY

`SVT_CMD_CLEAR_SEVERITY is a special case value that will remove a previously applied filter rather than establish a new filter.

is_valid - Functions as a return value ('0' if the handle argument does not point to a data object that is currently active, or if the property specified by the prop_name argument does not exist in that object, or if the property is an array but the index specified by the array_ix argument is out of bounds).

handle - Identifies the data object whose property is to be modified.

prop_name - Identifies the property name whose value is to be modified.

prop_val - Value to be applied to the property. Note: Regardless of its actual type in the data object, the property value must be set as a 1Kb bit-vector. Macro constant values must be used for enumerated tyep values.

array_ix - Specifies the array element to be modified if the property is an array. This argument is required, but is ignored if the property is not an array. If this argument is out of the array bounds in the object, an error is reported.

  task notify_wait_for  (  output bit is_valid , input string notify_name  ) 

Command Support: When called from the command, does not return until the specified Notify notification event occurs within the model. This happens when a specified notification point has been reached. At that time, the model indicates the notification by returning from this wait_for.

is_valid - Functions as a return value ('0' if the notify_name argument does not specify a notification that is available for the command to use).

notify_name - The name of an vmm_notify notification event configured in the transactor, and intended to be command accessible. The name should be of the form "NOTIFY_...".

  task cmd_callback_wait_for  (  output bit is_valid , inout int handle , input string cb_notify_name  ) 

Command Support: When called from the command, does not return until the specified Command Callback notification event occurs within the model. This happens when a specified command accessible callback point has been reached. At that time, the model copies the data object of interest (at that callback point) to a command owned data object, and assigns the handle inout argument with a pointer to that object. The command code may then access the properties of that object using the handle.

Note: If the component is reset while this command is still blocking (waiting for the transactor to reach the callback point), this command will return immediately with is_valid = 1 and handle = SVT_CMD_RESET_HANDLE. If a user's testbench can generate that type of behavior, they should check for those two values as an indication that a reset occurred while waiting, and respond appropriately.

Note: The Command code must complete all accesses to the object, and then call in zero simulation time either the cmd_callback_proceed() method or this method again, otherwise the model will report a fatal error.

If this method is called instead of cmd_callback_proceed(), it will instruct the model to proceed with processing after the specified callback point (potentially using the data object modified by the Command code), and then return when the specified Command Callback notification event occurs within the model again.

is_valid - Functions as a return value ('0' if the cb_notify_name argument does not specify a command callback notification that is available for the command to use).

handle - Functions as a return value that points to the data object for the specified callback. Additionaly, the input value may identify a handle that was returned by a previous call to cmd_callback_wait_for for which to automatically issue a call to cmd_callback_proceed before blocking until the specified notification event occurs within the model.

cb_notify_name - The name of a notification event configured in the transactor, and intended to be command accessible. The name should be of the form "NOTIFY_CB_...".

  task cmd_callback_proceed  (  output bit is_valid , input int handle , string cb_notify_name  ) 

Command Support: When called from the command, instructs the model to proceed with processing after the specified callback point (potentially using the data object modified by the command code).

is_valid - Functions as a return value ('0' if the cb_notify_name argument does not specify a command callback notification marking a callback at which the model is currently halted, pending this method).

handle - Identifies the handle that was in use by the command for this callback, so the transactor can now get rid of the corresponding command owned data object.

cb_notify_name - The name of a notification event configured in the transactor, and intended to be command accessible. The name should be of the form "NOTIFY_CB_...".
